title: Intellectual Property
audience: a law student in a U.S. JD program
purpose: Analyze copyright (subject matter, ownership, rights, infringement and fair use), patents (eligibility, novelty, nonobviousness, claims and infringement), trademarks (distinctiveness, registration, infringement and dilution) and trade secrets, including open questions about software and artificial intelligence.

blocks.deliverable: Decide whether five works are copyrightable.
Apply the four fair-use factors to two uses.
Week 7 midterm; analyze whether an invention is novel and nonobvious.
Compare patent and trade-secret protection for a client's process.
Apply the likelihood-of-confusion factors to two marks.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: IP audit: for a supplied start-up's products, brand and software, written for the course, write a 2,000-word memo on what can be protected, how, and the main infringement risks.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
